messages.content: In 8 gb ram why 7.8 is there where does 200mb goes in simple words

Great question. Here's the simple explanation:

### 💾 Why 8 GB RAM shows as **7.8 GB usable**:

Out of the 8 GB RAM, **some memory is reserved by the system hardware**, especially the **graphics (GPU)** and **firmware**.

---

### 🔍 Here's where the missing ~200 MB goes:

| **Reserved For**         | **What It Does**                          | **Approx. Usage** |
|--------------------------|-------------------------------------------|--------------------|
| 🖥️ Integrated Graphics    | Uses RAM as video memory (VRAM)           | 100–300 MB         |
| 🧠 BIOS / UEFI Firmware   | Low-level system firmware & hardware setup| ~10–50 MB          |
| 🧰 Other Hardware         | Like PCI devices, onboard chips, etc.     | ~10–30 MB          |

---

### 🧠 Why It Matters:
- This memory is **not available for Windows or apps**, but it's still **part of your physical RAM**.
- So your system **has** 8 GB RAM, but only **7.8 GB is free for use** by Windows and programs.

---

✅ **This is normal** and happens on all systems. Nothing is broken or missing.

Here’s a clear and simple difference between a **microcontroller** and a **microprocessor**:

---

| **Feature**              | **Microcontroller (MCU)** 🧠🔧             | **Microprocessor (MPU)** 🧠💻              |
|--------------------------|---------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
| **Definition**           | A small computer on a **single chip** with CPU, RAM, ROM, and I/O ports built-in | Just the **CPU** (central processing unit) – needs external components like RAM, ROM, etc. |
| **Usage**                | Used in **embedded systems** (watches, microwave, remote, etc.) | Used in **general-purpose computers** (PCs, laptops) |
| **Memory**               | RAM, ROM, Flash are **on the same chip** | RAM, ROM, and I/O devices are **external** |
| **Cost**                 | Cheaper 💰                              | More expensive 💵                         |
| **Power Consumption**    | Low 🔋 (designed for efficiency)            | High 🔌 (needs more power and cooling)     |
| **Speed**                | Slower (typically MHz range) ⏱️            | Faster (GHz range) ⚡                      |
| **Applications**         | Washing machines, toys, sensors, etc.       | Desktops, servers, mobile phones          |

---

### 💡 In short:
- **Microcontroller = All-in-one small chip for specific tasks.**
- **Microprocessor = Powerful brain, needs help from other chips.**
